cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: OK, Graham, so let's check we both know what we're supposed to be doing.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: So, for the university's open day, we have to plan a display on British life and

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: literature in the mid-19th century.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: That's right.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: But we'll have some people to help us find the materials and set it up, remember – for

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: the moment, we just need to plan it.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: Good. So have you gathered who's expected to come and see the display?

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: Is it for the people studying English, or students from other departments?

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: I'm not clear about it.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Nor me.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: That was how it used to be, but it didn't attract many people, so this year it's going to

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: be part of an open day, to raise the university's profile.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: It'll be publicised in the city, to encourage people to come and find out something of

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: what does on here.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: And it's included in the information that's sent to people who are considering applying

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: to study here next year.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: Presumably some current students and lecturers will come?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: I would imagine so, but we've been told to concentrate on the other categories of people.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: Right. We don't have to cover the whole range of 19th-century literature, do we?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: No, it's entirely up to us. I suggest just using Charles Dickens.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: That's a good idea.

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: Most people have heard of him, and have probably read some of his novels, or seen films

cues.speaker: HY
cues.text: based on them, so that's a good lead-in to life in his time.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Exactly.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: And his novels show the awful conditions that most people had to live in, don't they: he

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: wanted to shock people into doing something about it.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Yes, he campaigned for education and other social reforms, and gave talks, but I'm

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: inclined to ignore that and focus on the novels.
